title: perf(canary): enhance auto-detection and hysteresis rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Ariella Chen
release_notes: Enhanced performance canary auto-detection with hysteresis and adaptive thresholds; rollout guard policies now support automatic rollback and canary stabilization windows.
description: Context: We've seen intermittent latency regressions during canary rollouts caused by noise in short-lived traffic patterns and transient KV-cache thrashing. This PR improves the perf-canary detector by adding adaptive hysteresis, an explicit stabilization window, and improved signal aggregation to reduce false positives and prevent unnecessary rollbacks. Motivation: reduce noisy rollbacks and restore canary reliability so we can safely adopt more aggressive canary percentages and faster rollouts. Changes: - Add adaptive hysteresis: the detector now maintains short and long windows (P50/P95/P99) and only triggers if multiple windows exceed thresholds. - Stabilization window: after a threshold breach, the canary enters a stabilization window (configurable, default 5m) before triggering automatic rollback. - Auto-rollback and canary annotations: automatic rollback is performed via the same rollout controller; we add structured annotations and reason codes to the rollout record for easier debugging. - Improved aggregation: bucketed request-level metrics replaced with latency quantiles plus sample counts to improve statistical stability at low traffic. - Tunable sensitivity profiles: ops can select conservative/standard/aggressive sensitivity profiles per-service. - New chaos tests and perf-canary simulator: unit and integration tests plus a simulator to validate hysteresis behavior under bursty and steady regressions. - Console/dashboard updates: canary timeline now shows stabilization windows and reason codes, and the alerting rules were tuned to avoid duplicate pager noise. Implementation notes: - Detector algorithm: added a two-tier threshold check (short_window + long_window) and a minimum-sample check before evaluating. - Rollout controller: moved rollback decision logic into a dedicated GuardEvaluator component to keep controller side-effects minimal. - Backwards compatibility: defaults maintain previous behavior for services that don't opt in. Migration plan: rollout staged across low-risk services for two weeks, then enable org-wide. Related work: ENG-1729 (canary detector revamp), ENG-1942 (rollout controller refactor), SUP-4123 (customer reported noisy rollbacks). Checklist: - [x] Design doc and benchmarks updated - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf canary simulator added - [x] Dashboard patches included - [x] Changelogs and release notes drafted How to test locally: run tools/perf-canary/simulate.py --profile bursty --duration 600 and observe guard decisions. Follow-up: expose per-canary sensitivity via API and add rollout dry-run mode (tracked in ENG-2035).
